summary_review.wording_limit: hardware_mention_only describes the keyword match, not proof that actual code uses no newer feature. Source review remains required. Exact duplicate grouping does not clear stable-patch/semantic lineage or protected tasks.

superseded_ref_only_scan.finding: Initial --all-only scan omitted ref-less local commit objects. The updated metadata-root scan addresses this without fetching history; old receipt preserved.

discovery_limitations: The scanner inspects commit messages only. It misses relevant source/API changes with no selected keywords, and long multi-change commit messages can mix an API mention with unrelated edits. Mentions do not establish that a final changed unit uses that feature. Discovery tags are not availability evidence.

Metadata-root discovery includes selection and metadata-summary files. Mirrors with missing parents retain partial traversal output and direct verified commit-object roots; their nonzero traversal statuses and errors remain explicit. Neither this fallback nor nonzero counts establish complete history.

Inventory row and exact-commit counts above precede stable-patch or conceptual-lineage deduplication. Shared commit objects can appear in multiple mirrors; do not count these as independent training examples. The earlier335/310 snapshot remains preserved separately.

Metadata seeding examines only direct lane case-index/inventory/selection/metadata-summaries files under expansion-v4-hour, excluding deeper supplement metadata and all llama.cpp history outside this root. Commit-object type checking is conservative, but does not make discovery exhaustive.
The MLX mirror is shallow; max5000 is a per-mirror upper bound, not demonstrated historical coverage. There is no fresh remote inventory claim.

One of five selected commits is already a sealed v4 exact optimization example. Other four lack matching exact heads in the four bound canonical case indices; this is not semantic-family/protected-task clearance.
Initial four zero-byte failed patch captures are preserved. Successful retry receipts and all five actual patch hashes were checked; no missing patch is silently counted as reviewed.

The four new-by-v4-head records are teaching evidence, not trainable/compiled/validated rows. Full before/after reconstruction, licenses, protected identities/finite-operation screening, exact replay and canonical token lengths remain admission gates.

records.title: Cooperative-tensor template-type compatibility

teaching_points.statement: The three mma/mman helpers name operand types from the factory-expression decltype, then pass those aliases to get_destination_cooperative_tensor instead of decltype of the local ct_a/ct_b objects. This is a concrete compiler/template compatibility technique, not a claimed algorithmic speedup.
The stated motivating environment is a Mac OS 27 build failure. This title does not imply that macOS27 is the minimum supported runtime for the resulting kernel.

records.title: Shape-aware SDPA dispatch by zero padding

teaching_points.statement: For D72/D80, the change zero-pads Q/K/V to96, retains the caller-provided scale, calls NAX attention, and copies only the original output width back. Changing the scale to one derived from96 would alter the attention contract.

The copies carry explicit source/destination strides instead of falsely marking a narrow view into padded storage contiguous. Temporary lifetimes are registered with the command encoder.

records.title: Skip discarded SIMD-group MoE work without skipping barriers

teaching_points.statement: Move expert-row overlap bounds before the K loop and form sg_active from a nonempty intersection. Only an active SIMD group loads its A/B fragments and performs its local matrix work.

The surrounding threadgroup barriers remain outside sg_active. Teaching the distinction between SIMD-group-local work and threadgroup-cooperative synchronization is more important than applying a blanket early return.
Both affine and floating-format NAX gather kernels are changed; the accumulator is still initialized and original row-range stores retained.

records.title: Explicit Metal member-function receiver address spaces

teaching_points.statement: Repository documentation explains that Metal4.1 changes the implicit this address space from thread to __metal_generic. Returning a thread-qualified reference can then fail; a trailing thread qualifier constrains the member-function receiver.

evidence.quote: +    is ``__metal_generic`` rather than ``thread``. Member functions in Metal

teaching_points.statement: The repair propagates receiver qualifiers through member operators, constructors, accessors and declarations/definitions throughout kernel headers; it is not merely a return-type annotation.

evidence.quote: +  T operator()(T x, T y) thread {

teaching_points.statement: Both built-in and extension compilation add -Wmetal-addr-spaces so missing receiver qualifiers can be detected before they become errors on affected toolchains.

scoped_code_or_author_conditions: MLX documentation explicitly attributes receiver-address-space behavior to Metal4.1; universal OS/GPU minimum remainsunknown.

records.title: Keep SDK, language and deployment target separate

teaching_points.statement: Building with a new SDK does not alone opt a binary into NAX: the captured MLX build gate requires Metal>=400, SDK>=26.2 and deploymenttarget>=26.2. This is an explicit repository build policy at this revision.

If no deployment target is supplied, the patch sets it from the host OS, then passes -mmacosx-version-min into the Metal preprocessor version probe. The host OS, SDK and effective language version are printed separately.
The release matrix changes its new-OS package from26.0 to26.2 while retaining14/15 targets; JACCL gets its own SDK/deployment gates. This is not a blanket claim that all MLX needs macOS26.2.

scoped_code_or_author_conditions: At this revision, NAX precompiled-kernel gate: MLX_METAL_VERSION>=400 AND macOS SDK>=26.2 AND deploymenttarget>=26.2.
MLX minimumgeneralSDK/deployment checks remain14.0 in this patch; that is scopedbuildcode, not a current product recommendation.
